The plan's in the pane for you.

The call I'd want your read on: I gave it a thesis rather than treating it as eight unrelated photos. The season's actual reporting all points the same way — recognisable shapes worn loose, colour that grows out without a line — so the collection is titled **Undone on Purpose**, and every caption carries the same three spec lines ("ask for / best on / home routine") so a client can screenshot one and bring it in. That's the thing most lookbooks miss: they inspire but don't tell you what to say at the desk.

Two other choices worth flagging: the upkeep table is deliberately unglamorous, because it's the most useful page in a real lookbook and it buys credibility for the rest. And the eight looks are genuine current techniques — boyfriend bob, cloud bangs, spiced smudge, khaki bronde — cited to the trade and beauty press, not invented names.

Lune & Ash is fictional and labelled as such on the closing card, with all imagery specified as concept photography rather than client work.

If you'd rather it run cuts-only, or drop the service detail and go pure image with two-word captions, say so and I'll reshape it before we build.
